english: We thank you (formal) for reaching out.
tip: To thank for something use за (za) plus the accusative: за обращение (za obrashchenie = for reaching out) after Благодарим (blagodarim = we thank).

english: A new technology was developed by engineers.
tip: In a passive, the doer takes the instrumental: разработана инженерами (razrabotana = developed, inzhenerami = by engineers).

english: While studying at the university, he worked part-time.
tip: Учась (uchas = studying) is the verbal adverb of the reflexive учиться (uchitsya = to study), keeping the reflexive -сь (-s) ending.

target: Товары доставляются на дом в течение трёх дней.
english: Goods are delivered to your home within three days.
tip: в течение (v techenie = within) takes the genitive: в течение трёх дней (tryokh dney = of three days).

english: Having thought, he agreed.
tip: Gerunds ending in -в mark an action finished before the main verb: Подумав (podumav = having thought), then agreeing.

english: All seats are taken.
tip: Short passive participles agree like adjectives: places are plural, so заняты (zanyaty = taken) takes the plural -ы ending.

english: The medicine was invented by a scientist.
tip: In passives the doer goes in the instrumental case: учёным (uchyonym = by a scientist) after изобретено (izobreteno = invented).

english: One and a half hours until departure.
tip: Полтора (poltora = one and a half) is followed by the genitive singular: Полтора часа (poltora chasa = an hour and a half).

english: Working at home, he saves time.
tip: Gerunds ending in -я show action at the same time as the main verb: Работая (rabotaya = working) while he saves time.

english: Two children are playing in the yard.
tip: Collective numerals like Двое (dvoe = two) count groups of people and take the genitive plural: Двое детей (dvoe detey = two children).

english: I need two hundred grams of oil.
tip: After numbers грамм often keeps its short genitive plural: двести грамм (dvesti gramm = two hundred grams) in everyday speech.

target: Вернувшись из отпуска, мы начали работать.
english: Having returned from vacation, we started working.
tip: Reflexive verbs ending in -ся build the gerund with -вшись: Вернувшись (vernuvshis = having returned).

target: До встречи в понедельник, хороших выходных!
english: Until Monday, have a great weekend!
tip: The position word до (do = until) takes the genitive: До встречи (do vstrechi = until the meeting), the usual way to say see you.

target: Информация обновляется на сайте каждый час.
english: Information is updated on the website every hour.
tip: Adding -ся makes an ongoing passive with no named doer: обновляется (obnovlyaetsya = is being updated) needs no 'by whom'.

target: Не за что, обращайтесь в любое время.
english: Not at all, feel free to contact me anytime.
tip: Не за что (ne za chto = don't mention it) is the set reply to thanks, literally 'there is nothing to thank for'.

target: Хорошего вечера и приятного отдыха после трудного дня!
english: Have a good evening and pleasant rest after a hard day!
tip: Good wishes drop 'I wish you' and put the noun in the genitive: Хорошего вечера (khoroshego vechera = good evening).

target: К лету через эту реку построят новый мост.
english: By summer a new bridge will be built across this river.
tip: A plain they-form with no subject means 'will be done': построят (postroyat = they will build) reads as a bridge will be built.

english: We need to buy a liter of milk.
tip: After a measure word the substance goes in the genitive: литр молока (litr moloka = a liter of milk), showing the amount.

english: Both brothers study at the university.
tip: Оба (oba = both) takes the genitive singular noun, same as 2 to 4: Оба брата (oba brata = both brothers), not the plural.

english: Four months of winter can be harsh.
tip: After 2, 3, 4 the noun is genitive singular: Четыре месяца (chetyre mesyatsa = four months), never the plural form.

target: Лёжа на диване, он смотрел телевизор.
english: Lying on the couch, he watched TV.
tip: A few verbs form the -я gerund irregularly, giving Лёжа (lyozha = lying) instead of the regular lezha form.

target: Результаты экзамена будут объявлены на следующей неделе.
english: The exam results will be announced next week.
tip: Future passive uses будут (budut = will be) plus a short participle: будут объявлены (budut obyavleny = will be announced).

target: Извините за беспокойство, не могли бы вы помочь?
english: I apologize for troubling you, but could you help?
tip: Apologies use за (za = for) plus the accusative: Извините за беспокойство (izvinite za bespokoystvo = sorry for the trouble).

english: The twenty-first century is the century of technology.
tip: In compound ordinals only the final word changes: Двадцать первый (dvadtsat pervyy = twenty-first) puts the ending on the last part.

english: Both sisters work.
tip: Обе (obe = both) is the feminine form, matching сестры (syostry = sisters). Masculine or mixed groups take оба (oba).

english: She is fifty-five years old.
tip: Age uses the dative: Ей (yej = to her), not она (ona = she). Ей пятьдесят пять лет (yej pyatdesyat pyat let) means she is fifty-five.

english: Seven don't wait for one.
tip: Семеро (semero = seven) is a collective numeral for a group of people, an everyday alternative to plain семь (sem).

english: Like two drops of water (identical).
tip: Две (dve = two) is the feminine form because капли (kapli = drops) is feminine. Masculine and neuter nouns take два (dva).

target: Это мой первый день на работе.
english: This is my first day at work.
tip: Work takes на (na), not в (v): на работе (na rabote = at work). Russian uses на for some locations where English says at or in.

target: Этот мост построен сто лет назад.
english: This bridge was built a hundred years ago.
tip: Построен (postroyen = built) is a short passive participle and agrees with мост (most = bridge): masculine singular, so no ending.
